newsitem.title: Russia: Yeltsin shown on TV for first time since surgery.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin shown on TV for first time since surgery.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, walking stiffly but smiling and with colour in his cheeks, said on Wednesday he felt well compared to how he felt immediately after heart surgery.

In the first television pictures shown of him since his quintuple bypass operation on November 5, Yeltsin was shown walking slowly in the grounds of Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital with members of his family.
Asked how he felt, the 65-year-old Kremlin leader replied: "Compared to the first days after the operation, fine."
Yeltsin, clad in a fur hat, checked woollen scarf and a long black coat, walked along a pathway of the hospital grounds with his wife, one of his two daughters and his granddaughter.
He said doctors had removed the surgery stitches on Wednesday and he expected to return to work after a spell at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.
In a written version of the interview issued by RIA news agency, Yeltsin said he was in combative mood and would return to work after a spell in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.
"I am in fighting mood. I will probably stay in Barvikha for some time and then go back to work," Yeltsin said.
He said his his heart pains had abated. "I do not feel my heart, it is quite different to before the operation," he said.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Itar-Tass news agency that Yeltsin would leave hospital and move to his Barvikha residence outside Moscow on Thursday afternoon or on Friday.

Yeltsin told RIA he would ask every top official to account for his actions during his absence from the Kremlin, where he has spent little time since falling ill just before his re-election on July 3.
